task.description: WF-02 Step 5. Independently re-run the suite and re-derive every one of REQ-027's five acceptance criteria against the ACTUAL shipped code and live database state -- not against TEST-RUNNER's report, not against any prior gate's verdict, and not against the design artefact's or a moduledoc's claims about themselves. Per core-directives.md, RELEASE-VALIDATOR re-runs rather than trusting the report alone; that is the entire reason this step exists. Also check docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml for staleness, and review this run's forwarded-issue set for any mis-classified blocker.
acceptance_criteria: the full suite is independently re-run (several times, given ISS-0011's characterised flake) with real output quoted
each of REQ-027's 5 acceptance criteria is verified against actual code or live catalog state, with evidence stated separately per criterion
docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml are checked for staleness relative to what shipped
the forwarded-issue set is reviewed for any mis-classified blocker
a release decision record is written to docs/status/

result.summary:
WF-02 Step 5 release validation for REQ-027: PASS. Every verdict below was re-derived from primary evidence -- a live Postgres catalog, BEAM module reflection, real INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE behaviour, and this validator's own suite runs -- not from TEST-RUNNER's report, any earlier gate's verdict, the design artefact, or a moduledoc's claim about itself.

SUITE (independently re-run, 6 times, all unpinned per ISS-0011's settled "pinning buys nothing" conclusion). ALL SIX CLEAN: "Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)", exit 0 each; durations 33.3/32.2/30.1/29.3/24.2/22.7s. Zero failures of any kind, so ISS-0011's flake did not fire and there was no red to attribute (unremarkable at its recorded ~7.5% rate). Run 5 was executed deliberately AFTER the criterion-1 mutation was reverted, so green is confirmed on a restored tree. Baseline reconciled rather than asserted: 271 before REQ-027, and REQ-027's own two test files (test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs + schemas_test.exs) run alone produce exactly "Result: 36 passed" -- 271 + 36 = 307, no unexplained gap. Other gates re-run by this validator: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exit 0; the same with `--force` exit 0 (a real recompile -- "Compiling 43 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app", not a no-op against a warm _build); `mix format --check-formatted` exit 0.

LIVE-CATALOG METHOD. A real tenants row was inserted, a real tenant schema provisioned via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1, and replay_migrations/1 (REQ-022's own mechanism, the one criterion 1 names) invoked. Schema tenant_781572b14d9c4d58a740461bcce33f2b; dropped afterwards with its tenant_schemas registration and tenants row.

AC 1 -- both migrations schema-per-tenant via :prefix, applying cleanly: PASS. Both files exist and sort FK-safe (...193001 before ...193002); both are registered in @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (registration being the mandatory second half of the guard pattern). replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, [20260816120001..120006, 20260816163103, 20260816193001, 20260816193002]} -- nine versions, none skipped, no exception. information_schema.tables shows both REQ-027 tables INSIDE the tenant schema; <tenant_schema>.schema_migrations records all nine versions. Negative control: neither table present in public. That negative control is, on its own, the vacuous assertion ISS-0029 identifies, so the load-bearing evidence is a MUTATION run by this validator: changing `if prefix() do` to `if true do` in 20260816193001 makes test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs:493 FAIL ("a registered tenant-scoped migration created something in public when run with no :prefix", naming CreateProcessDefinitions; 12/13 passed, exit 2). Mutation reverted via git checkout; tree confirmed unmodified, no stray public table left.

AC 2 -- unique (name, version) AND partial unique on name WHERE status='active': PASS. pg_indexes: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_definition_version ... USING btree (name, version)" and "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_definition ... USING btree (name) WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)". SILENT-CORRECTNESS property settled behaviourally, not by inspection: two rows with the same name and different versions were inserted letting the column default supply status; both read back status = "draft" (lowercase, matching the predicate's case). First activation ACCEPTED; second activation REJECTED with {:rejected, :unique_violation, "uq_active_definition", "duplicate key value violates unique constraint uq_active_definition"}. count(*) WHERE status='active' = 1, so the partial index matches a real row rather than being inert. PD-03's single-active-per-name invariant is genuinely enforced.

AC 3 -- nullable stage AND partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL: PASS. information_schema.columns: stage | character varying | is_nullable=YES | column_default=NULL. pg_indexes: "CREATE INDEX idx_def_stage ... USING btree (stage) WHERE (stage IS NOT NULL)" -- partial and correctly NON-unique. Confirmed by insertion that an omitted stage lands as nil (the predicate depends on it). No CHECK constraint and no enum on stage, consistent with PD-07's open-ended text.

AC 4 -- FK to process_definitions.id with NO ON DELETE CASCADE + moduledoc says deliberate per PD-08: PASS. SILENT-CORRECTNESS property read straight from pg_constraint: conname=instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey, contype='f', confdeltype='a' (NO ACTION) -- not 'c'. pg_get_constraintdef emits no ON DELETE clause at all, and ref_schema is the tenant schema (so the %Reference{} prefix fallback works). Only two constraints on the table (that FK + the pkey), so no second cascading FK hides elsewhere. BEHAVIOURAL: a snapshot was inserted, then DELETE of its referenced definition was REJECTED with {:rejected, :foreign_key_violation, "instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey", ...}; snapshot count after = 1, parent count = 1. Nothing cascaded. Moduledoc half checked against the COMPILED docs chunk via Code.fetch_docs/1 (what actually shipped, not the .ex source): the section "## No `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `definition_id` (REQ-027 acceptance criterion 4)" states it is deliberate per PD-08's "FK without ON DELETE CASCADE" paragraph, and warns that R-Co's own 1106_iss0125 cascade migration is deliberately not ported.

AC 5 -- both moduledocs cite definition.md (PD-01/PD-07/PD-08): PASS, verified by Code.fetch_docs/1 rather than by grepping source, proving the text is a real @moduledoc that survived compilation. ProcessDefinition: 4329 bytes, contains "src/design/definition.md"/PD-01/PD-07/PD-08 all true. InstanceDefinitionSnapshot: 4512 bytes, same four all true. Citations are substantive, not keyword-stuffed -- each names which sub-sections were ported and points at the sibling module, so a reader arriving at either finds the whole set. requirements.yaml's separate "note explicitly in both moduledocs" scope instruction is also met (both carry a schema-only scope section naming REQ-028/029/030/033). Export surface read from __info__(:functions) rather than trusted from prose: ProcessDefinition exports [create_changeset/2, update_changeset/2]; InstanceDefinitionSnapshot exports [create_changeset/2] only -- no update path, matching its write-once claim.

STALENESS. docs/requirements.yaml: not stale. REQ-027 reads status: in_progress, correct at Step 5 (DOC-UPDATER flips it at Step 6). Description cross-checked column by column against the live catalog -- every enumerated process_definitions column present with the described nullability/default, and instance_definition_snapshots carries exactly the six named columns and no more, satisfying "no timestamps beyond snapshotted_at" structurally. One imprecision recorded, not filed: the description's column list omits tenant_id though the shipped table has it NOT NULL -- licensed by the same description's Decision B preamble, matching REQ-023's precedent, and its substantive consequence is already ISS-0025 (whose affected_files names docs/requirements.yaml). docs/status/requirement_status.yaml: not stale. Exactly one REQ-027 event (`started`, ORCH, 2026-08-16T19:20:25Z) at line 1961 of 1976, the last entry; the `done` event is Step 6's job. Append-only intact. Its recorded 271 baseline is corroborated by this run's 271 + 36 = 307 reconciliation.

FORWARDED-ISSUE SET (ISS-0024..0029 plus UPDATEs to ISS-0011/0018/0025). No mis-classified blocker. Each is about a different requirement's scope (ISS-0024 -> REQ-033; ISS-0025 -> REQ-030/REQ-025), about agent tooling/role files (ISS-0026, ISS-0018), about REQ-022's or REQ-024's modules (ISS-0027, ISS-0028), or about a claim whose underlying property is covered elsewhere (ISS-0029).

  ISS-0025 (#83), own view reached independently: correctly non-blocking for REQ-027, genuinely blocking for REQ-030/REQ-025. (1) No acceptance criterion mentions tenant_id and all five passed with the column in place. (2) The column impedes nothing REQ-027 ships -- rows were inserted, updated and constraint-tested against the live table by supplying it explicitly. (3) The precedent claim was CHECKED, not accepted: events, events_archive and instance_projections each carry `add :tenant_id, :binary_id, null: false` with no DB default (read from migrations 120001/120003/120005), so REQ-023 shipped this exact pattern and merged -- blocking REQ-027 would apply a standard REQ-023 was not held to. (4) Dispositive for a release gate: the failure mode is LOUD. An insert omitting tenant_id raises 23502 not_null_violation immediately; it cannot produce a mis-attributed row, which is strictly safer than R-Co's session-GUC DEFAULT that silently stamps a stale tenant. Nothing can ship broken-but-quiet on this path. One presentation note passed on rather than re-filed: SECURITY-REVIEWER's attribution-integrity argument (favouring option (c), since a derived tenant_id cannot disagree with the schema it is written into) is the strongest reasoning in the record but sits in an UPDATE block below three options presented as equals -- a weak model reading top-down may not reach it.

  ISS-0029 (#87), the specific check requested: the vacuous refute was reproduced independently (the same negative control returns [] against the live catalog, as it must), and then the question that matters was settled -- is the property covered anywhere, or is criterion 1 actually unverified? It IS covered, by the section-4 guard test at test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs:493, which iterates tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (confirmed to contain both REQ-027 modules, since the replay returned both versions), runs each migration with NO :prefix under synthetic never-before-applied probe versions so each change/0 genuinely executes, and asserts the full public table set is unchanged. Verified by mutation, not by reading -- see AC 1. So NO acceptance criterion is left actually unverified. What remains wrong is only the claim in the inline comment and test/specs/REQ-027.md:111-113, which present the vacuous refute as proof the :prefix mechanism works. Worth closing (a later reader could conclude coverage lives there and not notice if the real coverage were removed) but not a blocker.

  ISS-0028 was incidentally CONFIRMED accurate by this run's mutation: the guard test failed as designed and afterwards no stray public.process_definitions remained, because process_definitions IS in @later_tenant_scoped_tables -- the same run demonstrates both that the cleanup works for REQ-027's tables and that it is the hand-maintained list whose gap the issue describes for REQ-024's event_type_registry.

FORMATTING. `mix format --check-formatted` exit 0, but the project gate still does not cover priv/ (.formatter.exs inputs re-read this run: ["{mix,.formatter}.exs", "{config,lib,test}/**/*.{ex,exs}"]) -- that is pre-existing ISS-0016, now hiding all 15 migrations. To distinguish "REQ-027 shipped bad formatting" from "the gate never looked", both REQ-027 migrations were checked under a scratch-only formatter config carrying import_deps: [:ecto_sql] (the project's .formatter.exs was NOT modified): exit 0. No formatting defect shipped.

DB HYGIENE. The one tenant schema created was dropped along with its tenant_schemas registration and tenants row. Verified post-cleanup from the script and again from a separate psql process: only `public` remains in letflow_test2, 0 leftover rv-req027-* tenants, 0 rows in tenant_schemas, and no stray public.process_definitions or public.instance_definition_snapshots after the deliberate mutation. All work confined to the letflow_test2 partition (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2); letflow_test and letflow_dev untouched, no `docker compose up` issued, branch never changed, and no port-4000 :eaddrinuse (ISS-0015) collision occurred in any run. Scratch scripts were deleted after use.

NOTHING NEW BLOCKING FOUND. No new blockers, majors or minors. Two observations only, neither warranting a new ISS -- see result.issues.

issues.detail: Followed the run instruction: registry.json untouched. Recorded per core-directives.md's rule to flag doc drift as MINOR rather than silently pick a side. REQ-023's release record raised the identical point at 2026-08-16T18:37Z and it is still unresolved, so this is now a recurring rediscovery cost rather than a one-off. Not filed as a new ISS-NNNN: it is a protocol-text question for ORCH to settle in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, not a defect in REQ-027 or in any shipped code.

issues.title: docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-027 description enumerates process_definitions' columns without tenant_id, which the shipped table carries as NOT NULL
issues.detail: Not an unauthorised addition: the same description's preamble explicitly places the table 'under Decision B's general rule, same as every other tenant-owned table this stage adds', and REQ-023 shipped the identical pattern on events, events_archive and instance_projections (verified directly from priv/repo/migrations/20260816120001, ..120003, ..120005). No acceptance criterion constrains the column list. The substantive consequence -- that nothing supplies a value -- is already ISS-0025, whose affected_files names docs/requirements.yaml, so this is deliberately NOT filed separately to avoid duplicating an open issue. Recorded only so a future reader comparing the requirement text to the live table does not read the column as unauthorised.
